milestones.label: Leggett-Garg QRNG Demonstration
milestones.description: First experimental single-system certified randomness generation using Leggett-Garg temporal inequality violations, establishing SDI paradigm without entanglement resource at 3865 bits/s

milestones.label: Rotation Box Framework
milestones.description: Proof that quantum theory permits maximally general rotation correlations for spin 0, 1/2, 1 but is exceeded for spin ≥ 3/2, expanding the landscape of post-quantum correlation theories

milestones.label: Heterogeneous Network Implementation
milestones.description: Practical demonstration of fully heterogeneous prepare-and-measure quantum network supporting diverse user systems and quantum tasks, marking transition toward real-world deployment

milestones.label: High-Dimensional Multipartite Non-Locality Observed
milestones.description: First experimental observation of genuine high-dimensional multipartite non-locality using path-encoded photonic GHZ states with 3-4 photons

milestones.label: On-Chip Contextuality QRNG
milestones.description: Silicon photonic chip integration of KCBS contextuality-based quantum randomness certification marks transition from tabletop to integrated quantum devices

milestones.label: Generalized Measurement Incompatibility
milestones.description: Partial joint-measurability formalism unifies fragmented incompatibility literature and directly bounds device-independent cryptographic security parameters

milestones.label: Mbps-Scale SDI QRNG Under General Attacks
milestones.description: Continuous-variable heterodyne QRNG achieves 1.165 Mbps with finite-size security against correlated measurement strategies, demonstrating commercial-scale viability

interactions.description: P&M correlation characterization tools (NPA hierarchy, semidefinite bounds) directly feed security proofs and randomness certification protocols
P&M operational scenarios motivate formal development of contextuality witnesses and incompatibility measures as characterization tools
Contextuality inequalities (KCBS, Leggett-Garg) and incompatibility frameworks directly enable certification proofs for SDI QRNG and QKD protocols
Non-contextual inequality violation tools and dimension witnesses feed high-dimensional device certification methodologies
High-dimensional OAM and GHZ experimental platforms provide concrete instantiations that refine and validate P&M theoretical bounds
High-dimensional quantum witnesses and robust certification protocols strengthen the physical assumptions underlying SDI security proofs
Practical SDI implementation results feed back requirements and constraints into P&M network protocol design

emergence_decline.description: Recognition that spin-bounded correlations require frameworks beyond standard Bell/CHSH inequalities for characterizing higher-spin quantum systems
Silicon photonic platform maturation enables chip-scale contextuality exploitation for certified randomness generation
Demand for higher-capacity quantum communication drives extension of qubit entanglement swapping and certification to qudit systems
Binary incompatibility framework found insufficient for capturing partial classical determinism in complex multi-outcome measurements

emergence_decline.field: Weak-Value QKD as Distinct Security Paradigm
emergence_decline.description: Formal proof that removing WMA approximation provides no genuine security advantage dissolves weak-value QKD as a distinct sub-field, absorbing it into standard QKD security analysis

current_state_summary: As of 2026, Quantum Matrix Computation research is converging on a semi-device-independent paradigm where prepare-and-measure frameworks serve as the unifying operational scaffold, contextuality and measurement incompatibility supply the formal certification machinery, and high-dimensional photonic platforms (OAM, GHZ states, temporal lattices) provide the experimental substrate. The field is rapidly transitioning from proof-of-concept demonstrations toward integrated silicon photonic implementations and Mbps-scale randomness generation resistant to general attacks. The next stage appears to involve fully heterogeneous multi-user quantum networks where robust high-dimensional device certification and SDI security co-evolve as complementary requirements for practical quantum information infrastructure.
